title: A Typewriter for the Atlas
premise: In 1919, in a border town where the armistice is being negotiated, Isandro Underhill lives as her late brother to keep her father's print shop open, cutting type by day and forging travel permits by night for neighbors fleeing the requisitioning army. When soldiers seize the town's ledger of names — including every family Isandro has smuggled out — she must forge one final document granting a single berth on the last evacuation train before the armistice is signed. Torn between her dying father, the printer's apprentice she loves, and the orphaned boy who knows her secret, she chooses to give up her own berth, staying behind to reprint the stolen names from memory so the disappeared cannot vanish twice. The armistice holds; the train leaves without her; but her printed list forces the commission to account for the taken, and she survives the occupation long enough to see her father's type set her name in ink.
about_author: I. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring obsolete printing equipment in Eastern European archives before turning to fiction. They write about ordinary people whose small crafts become instruments of resistance.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Isandro, dressed as her dead brother Tomás, cuts type in her father's print shop while the town whispers of approaching armies. POV: Isandro. Beat: quiet dread beneath routine; establish her double life and the shop as sanctuary.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Father Underhill insists every job be recorded in the shop ledger — names, payments, favors. Isandro realizes the ledger is evidence of her forgeries. POV: Isandro. Beat: first crack in safety; love interest Mateo arrives with a request that isn't about type.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Army officers post notices: the town is commandeered, all records surrendered within three days. The ledger must go. POV: Isandro. Beat: panic converted into resolve; she begins copying names onto rice paper hidden in type cases.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Neighbors bring valuables to hide; Isandro weighs each object against what can be carried on foot. Her father coughs blood into a handkerchief he thinks she doesn't see. POV: Isandro. Beat: tenderness sharpened by scarcity.

chapters.title: Mateo's Hands
chapters.summary: Mateo, the apprentice, catches Isandro forging a permit and instead of betraying her, asks to learn. A charged night at the press. POV: Mateo. Beat: intimacy born of complicity; love declared sideways through craft.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counted Soldiers
chapters.summary: Ferren, an orphan who loiters outside counting troop movements, reveals he knows 'Tomás' is a girl. He wants passage out in exchange for silence. POV: Ferren. Beat: blackmail that curdles into unexpected loyalty.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: A checkpoint inspection nearly exposes the hidden papers; Father covers for Isandro and collapses afterward. The doctor says weeks, not months. POV: Isandro. Beat: guilt and gratitude braided together; stakes turn personal and mortal.

chapters.title: The Commission Arrives
chapters.summary: Armistice negotiators billet in the town; among them a clerk who once bought type from Underhill and remembers 'Tomás' fondly. POV: Isandro. Beat: dangerous hope — an inside thread to the commission.

chapters.title: Berths on the Last Train
chapters.summary: Rumor hardens into fact: one evacuation train before signing, limited berths, lists drawn by the occupying command. Isandro counts her family against the number. POV: Mateo. Beat: arithmetic of sacrifice begins.

chapters.title: The Stolen Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro infiltrates the requisition office at night and confirms the ledger sits in the commission's archive — every name she saved now a list of the hunted. POV: Isandro. Beat: cold clarity; the enemy is paperwork, not just men.

chapters.title: Father's Bargain
chapters.summary: Father, lucid for an evening, offers his own berth to whoever needs it most and asks Isandro to promise the shop's type will outlive them both. POV: Father (close third). Beat: inheritance reframed as duty, not property.

chapters.title: Permits for Strangers
chapters.summary: Demand for forged papers triples; Mateo and Isandro work until their fingers split. Ferren runs messages. The network becomes a family none of them chose. POV: Mateo. Beat: solidarity's warmth before the cost arrives.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bakery
chapters.summary: A neighbor caught with a false permit names the print shop under interrogation. Soldiers seal the premises; Isandro hides the remaining blanks inside hollow type sorts. POV: Isandro. Beat: the noose tightens; trust becomes currency she can't mint.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Tomás Underhill
chapters.summary: Questioned as her brother, Isandro performs masculinity under a lamp while the clerk from the commission watches, saying nothing. POV: Isandro. Beat: terror and a flicker of ambiguous protection.

chapters.title: What Ferren Saw
chapters.summary: Ferren witnesses the neighbor's execution and goes mute. Isandro cares for him; he finally speaks only to ask if his name will be in the book. POV: Ferren. Beat: grief given language; the moral center of the story.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: The berth list is finalized: three names, one seat. Father is too ill to survive the journey without her; Mateo refuses to leave; Ferren has no claim at all. POV: Isandro. Beat: the choice crystallizes into unbearable geometry.

chapters.title: The Night Before Signing
chapters.summary: Isandro sets type by candlelight: a broadside listing every name from memory, to be posted when the commission signs. Mateo begs her to take the berth; she has already decided otherwise. POV: Mateo. Beat: love against duty, argued and unresolved.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: At the platform, Isandro gives the berth to Ferren, forging his name onto the manifest. Mateo stays with her. The train pulls out as church bells mark the hour of signing. POV: Isandro. Beat: climax of sacrifice; heartbreak held upright by purpose.

chapters.title: Broadside
chapters.summary: As delegates sign across the river, Isandro and Mateo paste the broadside of names on the commission's own door. The clerk recognizes the typeface and does not tear it down. POV: Isandro. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered in ink.

chapters.title: Accounted For
chapters.summary: The published names force inquiries; some of the taken are found, most are not, but none can be erased. The occupiers withdraw rather than answer for the list. POV: Mateo. Beat: victory measured honestly — partial, real.

chapters.title: Setting Her Name
chapters.summary: Father dies at peace as Isandro composes the shop's final job: a memorial page bearing every name, including his, including hers as Isandro, not Tomás. POV: Isandro. Beat: identity reclaimed through craft; mourning made public.

chapters.title: A Typewriter for the Atlas
chapters.summary: Years later, Ferren returns grown, carrying a typewriter salvaged from the train, and finds the shop reopened under Isandro and Mateo's names. She sets his name in lead. POV: Isandro. Beat: resolution — survival's price paid, love kept, memory typeset forever.
